title: Adjustment disorder
description: Adjustment disorder is a maladaptive reaction to an identifiable psychosocial stressor or multiple stressors (e.g. divorce, illness or disability, socio-economic problems, conflicts at home or work) that usually emerges within a month of the stressor. The disorder is characterised by preoccupation with the stressor or its consequences, including excessive worry, recurrent and distressing thoughts about the stressor, or constant rumination about its implications, as well as by failure to adapt to the stressor that causes significant impairment in personal, family, social, educational, occupational or other important areas of functioning. The symptoms are not better explained by another mental disorder (e.g., Mood Disorder, another Disorder Specifically Associated with Stress) and typically resolve within 6 months, unless the stressor persists for a longer duration.

essentialFeatures: A maladaptive reaction to an identifiable psychosocial stressor or multiple stressors that usually emerges within a month of the stressor.

The reaction to the stressor is characterized by preoccupation with the stressor or its consequences, including excessive worry, recurrent and distressing thoughts, or constant rumination about its implications.
The symptoms are not better accounted for by another mental disorder.
Once the stressor and its consequences have ended, the symptoms resolve within 6 months.
Failure to adapt to the stressor results in significant impairment in personal, family, social, educational, occupational, or other important areas of functioning.
additionalClinicalFeatures: Symptoms of preoccupation may worsen with reminders of the stressor, resulting in avoidance of stimuli, thoughts, feelings, or discussions associated with the stressor.
Additional psychological symptoms may include depressive or anxiety symptoms as well as impulsive externalizing symptoms, particularly increased tobacco, alcohol, or other substance use.
Symptoms usually abate when the stressor is removed, sufficient support is provided, or additional coping mechanisms are developed.
boundaryWithNormality: Represents a maladaptive reaction and failure to adapt to a stressor that is associated with significant preoccupation and impairment.
Emotional reactions to negative life events that do not meet these requirements should not be diagnosed as Adjustment disorder.
Symptoms that occur as transient responses and resolve within a few days do not typically warrant a diagnosis.
In cases where responses to traumatic events are considered normal given the severity of the stressor, Acute Stress Reaction may be assigned.
courseFeatures: Onset usually occurs within a month after exposure to a stressful life event, though onset can be delayed.
Acute and intense stressors typically result in rapid onset and shorter duration, whereas persistent stressors may lead to delayed onset and longer duration.
The intensity and duration of the disorder varies widely.

children: Preoccupation with a stressor or its consequences may manifest through somatic symptoms, disruptive or oppositional behaviour, hyperactivity, tantrums, concentration problems, irritability, increased clinginess, regression, bedwetting, or sleep disturbances when persistent.
adolescents: Behavioural manifestations can include substance use and various forms of acting out or risk-taking.
olderAdults: Preoccupation with somatic complaints is common; individuals often express greater anxiety about health, report significant demoralization, and display persistent somatization of psychological symptoms.

cultureRelatedFeatures: May be exacerbated in the context of limited family or community support, particularly in collectivistic or sociocentric cultures.
Symptoms may be influenced by local idioms associated with fear or preoccupation with stressors that have strong cultural connotations.

boundariesWithOtherDisordersAndCondition.title: Boundary with Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
boundariesWithOtherDisordersAndCondition.description: In Adjustment disorder, the stressor can be of any severity and is not necessarily extremely threatening or horrific. Diagnosis depends on whether the full requirements for either disorder are met, not solely on the type of stressor.

boundariesWithOtherDisordersAndCondition.title: Boundary with other mental disorders
boundariesWithOtherDisordersAndCondition.description: Stressful life experiences commonly trigger or exacerbate other mental disorders. Adjustment disorder should generally not be assigned when another mental disorder accounts for the symptoms, unless the symptomatology is substantially non-overlapping and both full diagnostic requirements are met. If symptoms persist for more than 6 months after the stressor ends, another diagnosis is typically more appropriate.
